name: What Should a Kitchen Renovation Contract Include to Prevent Change Orders?

mainEntity.name: Which kitchen remodel details should be written into a San Diego contractor’s contract before work starts?
mainEntity.text: Which kitchen remodel details should be written into a San Diego contractor’s contract before work starts?

acceptedAnswer.text: The contract should describe the finished kitchen precisely enough that another professional could understand the scope. Include plans, dimensions, cabinet construction, finish, hardware, countertop material and edge, backsplash, flooring, paint, appliances, lighting, plumbing fixtures, ventilation, and trim. List every allowance with a quantity or dollar amount, including appliances, tile, hardware, fixtures, and countertops. Identify exclusions such as structural repairs, panel upgrades, asbestos or lead-related work, floor leveling, wall repairs, permit fees, and appliance delivery. State the payment schedule, start conditions, estimated completion period, inspection responsibilities, cleanup standards, protection for occupied rooms, and warranty process. Require written change orders showing the reason, added or credited cost, schedule impact, and approval deadline. Clarify who orders materials and who absorbs costs caused by measurement errors, damaged products, or incorrect quantities. Reviews of remodeling projects often mention missing cabinets, tile shortages, delayed materials, and poor communication, so the contract should assign responsibility for verification and provide a defined communication routine.
acceptedAnswer.description: A detailed contract should identify drawings, materials, appliance models, allowances, labor, permits, inspections, exclusions, payment milestones, schedule assumptions, cleanup, warranty terms, and change-order procedures. It should also state who handles design revisions, damaged materials, utility upgrades, and concealed conditions. Never rely on verbal promises for layout, finish quality, or completion dates.
